topic: Beginner mistake: clicking "Yes, don't ask again" without reading (and the /rewind safety net)
post:
The riskiest button for Claude Code beginners? 🚦
"Yes, don't ask again."

Claude Code asks your permission before it does things like editing files or running commands. (A "command" is a typed instruction your computer runs.)

That pop-up is your seatbelt. Here's how to use it well 👇

1️⃣ Read it before you click
It tells you exactly what Claude wants to do. If you don't understand it, ask: "Explain that in plain English first."

2️⃣ Save "don't ask again" for harmless things
For a command, that choice is saved for the whole project, including future sessions. Type /permissions to see and change what you've allowed.

3️⃣ Know your undo button ⏪
Press Esc twice (or type /rewind) to roll Claude's file edits back to an earlier point.

4️⃣ Know its limit
Rewind doesn't undo changes made by commands, like deleting a file. So work on a copy of anything important. 🗂️

Why it matters:
The permission prompt isn't a speed bump. It's the moment you stay in charge. A 5-second read beats an hour of cleanup. 💡

Do you read the pop-ups, or click straight through? 👇

Follow me: I'm teaching one Claude skill a day, no tech background needed.
